script: I-9 and background check requirements by worker type. Not every person you bring on needs the same checks. Federal law requires a Form I-9 for every employee, and Vanderbilt requires background checks for some worker types. Get it wrong, and you either delay a start, or start someone without required clearance.
Identify the worker type first: student worker, staff, faculty, campus affiliate, or a service free stipend or student expense only appointment. The type sets which checks apply.

Know who counts as each type. Only Vanderbilt students hold a student relationship. Other interns are set up as postdocs, temporary staff, or term staff. Campus affiliates can be independent contractors, employees of contracted vendors, or non-compensated affiliates.

Then look up the requirement. Paid employees need an I-9. Staff and faculty also need a background check. Affiliates need a background check only. Service free stipend and student expense only appointments need neither.
The employee completes I-9 Section 1 by the first day of work for pay. It can be done any time after the offer is accepted.
Section 2 is due within three business days of the start date, after the employer reviews the documents in person. Start Monday, and Section 2 is due Thursday.
When a background check applies, wait for clear to start. P E B C clears the check, run through HireRight, and emails you. Don't start the person before that email.
No requisition? Staff checks on requisitions are automated in Oracle Recruiting. Other populations need a manual request through Formstack.
Two things to remember. Section 1 can't wait for the three-day window: it's due on day one. And New York requires non-criminal background checks before any conditional offer.
